title: Teddy Wilson and Roy Eldridge in Speed Webb's band
summary: Teddy Wilson already showed something in Speed Webb's band, playing on the order of Earl Hines, and Roy Eldridge played fast like Rex Stewart with his own ideas.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, it isn't everybody who turns out to be a great musician who has it all together at that age. Probably, say, for instance, when you were working with Teddy Wilson, and Teddy was pretty young then, in Speed Webb's band... Did he sound...
Did Teddy sound then, when you worked with him in Speed Webb's band... Was he already showing something...?
Yes. He played on the order of Earl Hines at that time. Which he did retain some of that right on still, you know.
It's funny. We was talkin' about him yesterday, and he was right on TV. Isn't that a funny thing?
Yeah, it was. That was quite a coincidence. And Roy, how was he sounding then?
Great. Roy played fast like Rex. Rex at that time was one of the fastest trumpet players. And Roy sounded a whole lot like Rex, only Roy had his own original stuff, you know. But he...
Because you know, he usually says he wasn't really listening to Louis then yet. It wasn't until a little after that that he became aware of Louis, and sort of got a story as well as speed.
